howItWorks.title: One fund, three sides.
howItWorks.intro: A fund is a shared pot of money — built from member contributions, dues, donations, or grants — that pays out to the people and businesses keeping things running, whether that's local merchants, suppliers, your club's bar, or your space's event vendors. La caisse runs the whole loop, from members and contributors in to payouts out.

members.title: Members receive and spend.
members.body: Members register through your fund's onboarding form and get a balance that's theirs to use — credited through allocations, dues, top-ups, or contributions, depending on how your fund works. They use a card to spend at participating merchants and suppliers. They can add cards for dependents, report a lost card, check their balance, and invite others with a referral code that rewards them when the new member activates.

team.title: Your team runs the fund.
team.body: You set the rules: how money flows in and out, on what cadence, and with what structure. Solidarity funds typically configure tiered allocations; clubs configure dues; community spaces configure memberships. La caisse handles the rest — onboarding new members, sending reminders, flagging missed payments or contributions, and giving you a live dashboard of balances, payouts, and per-supplier activity.

merchants.title: Merchants and suppliers get paid.
merchants.body: The people and businesses you pay — local merchants, suppliers, your club's bar, your space's event vendors — register with your fund and connect a Citizen Pay account. When money's owed to them, La caisse pays out on the cycle you set, minus any fee your fund configures. They see incoming payments, fees, and payout history from their own dashboard.

howItWorks.loopCaption: Contributions and dues fund the pot. Members use what they're owed. Suppliers and merchants get paid. Reports show every step.

multiTenant.title: Your fund. Your brand. Your rules
multiTenant.intro: La caisse is built so every fund runs as its own product. Members never see a generic platform — they see your fund. Behind the scenes, the platform stays consistent so funds can share improvements, run on shared infrastructure, and avoid the maintenance burden of a true fork.

yours.heading: Yours to configure.
yours.description: Everything members and merchants encounter as "your fund."

customDomain.title: Custom domain
customDomain.body: Run on votrecaisse.org or a subdomain of the official instance. SSL handled, no configuration required.

logoAndColor.title: Logo and brand color
logoAndColor.body: Upload your logo, pick a primary color. Buttons, links, highlights, transactional emails — the interface picks up your color automatically.

tokenName.title: Token name
tokenName.body: Call your fund's currency whatever fits — solidaire, panier, credit, ticket. It appears in every balance, transaction, and email.

registrationForm.title: Registration form
registrationForm.body: Build the onboarding form your fund needs. Household composition, income tier, neighborhood, GDPR consent — your fields, your validation, your order.

terms.title: Terms and conditions
terms.body: Your terms, displayed during onboarding and accessible from every member account. Versioned, with re-acceptance prompts when you update them.

allocationRules.title: Allocation rules
allocationRules.body: Configure how money flows — allocation tiers for solidarity funds, dues for clubs, memberships for community spaces. Cadence, amounts, and tier assignment all stay under your control. Your policy, codified.

language.title: Interface language
language.body: EN, FR, or NL today. Members see your fund's language by default; bilingual funds can let members choose.

merchantFees.title: Merchant fees
merchantFees.body: Set the fee structure that works for your fund and your merchants — flat percentage, per-transaction, or hybrid.

shared.heading: Shared across all funds.
shared.description: The structural choices that let funds share improvements and stay reliable.

coreMechanics.title: Core mechanics
coreMechanics.body: The way allocations, payouts, and member accounts work is the same everywhere. When one fund finds a better way, every fund gets it.

pageStructure.title: Page structure and navigation
pageStructure.body: Members and merchants who use one fund recognize another. Familiar layout, familiar flows.

typography.title: Typography and spacing
typography.body: Typeface, type sizes, spacing scale, and component shapes are fixed. Tenants choose color and logo; the rest stays consistent.

security.title: Security and infrastructure
security.body: Authentication, session handling, audit logging, GDPR controls, encryption — not configurable per fund, because there's no good reason for them to vary.

paymentIntegration.title: Payment integration
paymentIntegration.body: Citizen Pay is the merchant payment rail. Alternative integrations may come, but each fund doesn't get to bring their own.

hosting.title: Run by us, or run by you.
hosting.subtitle: Two paths, same software.

path1.label: OFFICIAL INSTANCE
path1.title: Hosted by Citizen Pay.
path1.body: We provision your fund, handle hosting and updates, and run the infrastructure. You focus on your members. €20/month flat — free for registered non-profits and schools.

path2.label: SELF-HOSTED
path2.title: Run it yourself.
path2.body: AGPL-3.0 licensed, deploy on your own Vercel account or anywhere Next.js runs. You handle hosting and updates; you keep full control. Free.

features.intro: Built from years of running real funds — starting with La CLASS — and shaped for the solidarity funds, clubs, and community spaces that come next. Grouped by who's using it.

members.label: For your members
members.intro: A simple account, a card, and a balance that's clearly theirs.

accountsCards.title: One account, multiple cards.
accountsCards.body: Members register once and can add cards for dependents — a partner, a child, anyone in the household covered by the fund. Lost or stolen cards can be blocked from the app in seconds.

allocations.title: Money moves on schedule.
allocations.body: Members see their balance change on the cadence your fund sets — weekly, monthly, or otherwise. Reminders nudge them before each cycle so nothing's missed.

balance.title: Always know where things stand.
balance.body: Current balance, full history, recent spending at each merchant. Everything members need, nothing they don't.

referrals.title: Members grow the fund.
referrals.body: Every member gets an invite code. When someone joins and activates through their code, the referring member is rewarded — at an amount your fund configures.

team.label: For your team
team.intro: The controls to run the fund and the visibility to know it's working.

tieredAllocations.title: Allocate by situation, not by formula.
tieredAllocations.body: Configure target, minimum, and maximum amounts that adapt to each member's situation — household size or income for solidarity funds, age or category for clubs, plan tier for community spaces. Members in different tiers contribute or receive differently, automatically.

memberManagement.title: Onboarding, activation, and the boring parts handled.
memberManagement.body: Registration form (yours to design), account activation, address changes, card replacements — all in one place, all auditable.

reporting.title: See the whole fund at a glance.
reporting.body: Total balance, balance by tier, payouts per merchant or supplier, recent activity. Export what you need for your annual report or your funder.

transactionalEmail.title: The right message at the right moment.
transactionalEmail.body: Confirmation when a member joins, reminders before cycles, alerts when something goes wrong. All sent automatically, all branded to your fund.

merchants.label: For merchants and suppliers
merchants.intro: A clean integration that doesn't ask the people you pay to learn a new tool.

onboarding.title: Sign up once, get paid forever.
onboarding.body: Merchants and suppliers connect a Citizen Pay account during onboarding. No card readers to install, no monthly logins required.

fees.title: Your fund sets the rules.
fees.body: Define a fee — a flat percentage or a per-transaction amount — and it's deducted automatically at payout. Recipients see the breakdown on every transaction.

payouts.title: Money lands when expected.
payouts.body: Set a payout cycle that works for your suppliers and the fund's cash flow. Recipients get a clear view of incoming payments, fees, and what's owed.

underTheHood.title: And the parts you don't see.
underTheHood.body: Multi-tenant from the ground up, GDPR-conscious by design, open source under AGPL-3.0. Every fund runs in isolation, with its own data, its own branding, and its own configuration — on shared infrastructure or your own.

left.title: Start a fund in an afternoon.
left.body: Set up your subdomain, invite your first members, onboard your first merchants and suppliers. Plain English, sensible defaults. €20/month — free for registered non-profits and schools.

right.title: Self-host on your own box.
right.body: Pull the image, run the migration, point a domain. AGPL-3.0 on GitHub.

footer.description: Open-source infrastructure for local solidarity funds, clubs, and community spaces. Hosted by us, or self-hosted on your own server.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.intro: This notice explains what personal data La caisse collects, why we process it, and what choices you have. It applies to people who visit lacaisse.eu, hold an account, operate a fund hosted by us, or participate as a member, merchant, or guest of a fund we host.

controller.heading: Who we are
controller.body: La caisse is operated by Citizen Pay BV, a Belgian company with registered office at Cantersteen 47, 1000 Brussels, company number 1029.985.788, VAT BE 1029.985.788. Citizen Pay BV is the data controller for the personal data described in this notice. You can reach us at privacy@lacaisse.eu.

scope.heading: When this notice applies
scope.intro: We process personal data when you:
items: visit lacaisse.eu or a fund subdomain we operate;
create or hold a La caisse account;
operate a fund on our hosted infrastructure; or
participate as a member, merchant, or guest of a fund we host.
scope.note: If you participate in a fund operated by a third party who self-hosts La caisse, that operator is the controller for your data — not us.

data.heading: What we collect and why
data.intro: We process the following categories of personal data:
items: Account data — name, email, password hash, passkey credentials. To provide and secure your account (GDPR art. 6.1.b — contract).
Fund operational data — fund name, branding, members, allocation rules, transactions. To run the fund on your behalf (contract; processor on behalf of the fund operator).
Billing data — payment tokens, invoices, VAT numbers. To process subscription payments and meet accounting obligations.
Usage logs — IP, browser, session activity. For security, abuse prevention, and debugging (legitimate interest, art. 6.1.f).
Support correspondence — emails and messages you send us. To respond to your queries (legitimate interest).
Marketing emails — only if you opt in, withdrawable at any time (consent, art. 6.1.a).
data.note: For member data processed on behalf of a fund operator, we act as a processor. The fund operator is the controller and decides retention, access, and disclosure for that data.

subprocessors.heading: Sub-processors
subprocessors.intro: We rely on the sub-processors below to operate the service:
items: Vercel Inc. — application hosting (EU; US transfers under Standard Contractual Clauses).
Supabase Inc. — database, authentication, storage (EU region).
Resend Inc. — transactional and notification email (EU; US transfers under SCCs).
Citizenpay — open banking and token settlement (EU).
subprocessors.note: Transfers to the United States rely on Standard Contractual Clauses and the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework where applicable. An up-to-date sub-processor list is available on request.

retention.heading: How long we keep your data
items: Account data: while your account is active, plus 30 days after closure.
Fund operational data: while the fund is active. After closure, exportable for 30 days, then deleted within 90 days.
Billing records: 7 years (Belgian accounting law).
Logs: 30 to 90 days depending on category.

rights.heading: Your rights
rights.intro: Under the GDPR you have the right to:
items: access the personal data we hold about you;
have inaccurate data corrected;
have data erased, subject to retention obligations;
restrict or object to processing;
receive your data in a portable format;
withdraw any consent you have given;
lodge a complaint with the Belgian Data Protection Authority at www.dataprotectionauthority.be.
